mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Mon 4:06 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-16 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc
items.about: AST SpaceMobile is building a satellite network designed to connect directly to ordinary smartphones.
items.why: Shares fell about 12% and kept sliding after the bell, the biggest drop on the board. Posts say SpaceX's launch backlog has pushed back the BlueBird 14–16 and 17–19 missions, and they circulated an Ars Technica piece doubting AST's plan to build its own reusable rocket within two years. AST's Nov 10 update had already pushed its target of about 45 satellites in orbit to mid-2027, with the next batch still waiting on a SpaceX launch date.

items.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co
items.about: JPMorgan Chase is the largest U.S. bank, with consumer banking, investment banking, asset management and payments businesses.
items.why: JPM fell 2.3% as the broad market sold off (S&P 500 -1.9%) and customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo reported online and app outages, according to a CBS News report shared on the stream. Posts speculate about cyberattacks or a bank run, but nothing official confirmed either claim by the close.

items.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
items.about: Take-Two publishes video games through labels including Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto), 2K and Zynga.
items.why: Take-Two rose to about $238 early, then reversed to close down 6.3% at $213 on roughly 4.8 million shares, three days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, Nov 19. No company news explained the drop. Posts blame worries about pre-launch sales and call it a 'sell the news' move ahead of release.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc
items.about: SELLAS is a clinical-stage biotech developing cancer immunotherapies, led by galinpepimut-S (GPS) for acute myeloid leukemia.
items.why: SLS swung between $7.24 and $8.35 and closed down 5%, while traders waited for topline results from the Phase 3 REGAL trial of GPS. The trial hit its 80th event on Oct 28, which triggers the final analysis, and SELLAS has guided to preliminary overall-survival results this quarter. No new release had come out by the close.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Nvidia designs GPUs and networking hardware that power most AI data centers, plus gaming and automotive chips.
items.why: Nvidia fell 4.1% to $156 on 277 million shares, dragging the Nasdaq lower the day before it reports earnings after the close Tuesday, Nov 17. This is its first report since CEO Jensen Huang's exit last week. Posts cite a CNBC report that the board is not considering bringing Huang back, and a post citing Yahoo Finance puts the consensus at about $108.7B in revenue (+91% year on year) and $2.47 adjusted EPS.

items.name: Helus Pharma Inc.
items.about: Helus Pharma develops psychedelic-derived treatments for depression, led by its psilocybin-based candidate HLP003.
items.why: HELP fell 13% after its late-stage APPROACH depression trial of HLP003 met its main goal, but the earnings call disclosed three treatment-related serious adverse events, one of them a suicide attempt, according to Stocktwits News. Posts relay a Barclays note that keeps an Overweight rating and calls the efficacy a 'home run'. Investors are asking for details on the other two events. The company had guided to APPROACH topline data in Q4 2026.

items.name: Omeros Corp
items.about: Omeros is a biopharma company that sells YARTEMLEA, a treatment for transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy, and develops complement-pathway drugs.
items.why: Omeros closed down 4.6%, then fell about another 6% to $15.64 after the bell when it released Q3 results, with a 4:30 p.m. ET call. Posts trade quarterly YARTEMLEA sales figures of roughly $35–42M and argue over whether the quarter beat expectations. For comparison, Q2 YARTEMLEA net revenue was $28.5M.

items.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
items.about: SPY is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 index of large U.S. companies.
items.why: SPY fell 1.9% to about $740 in a steady slide, led by Nvidia (-4%) and the banks, with traders citing the outages at major banks and nerves before Nvidia reports Tuesday. Posts point to the VIX climbing from about 20 to 24 and to $740 as a support level that held at the close.

items.name: fuboTV Inc
items.about: Fubo runs a sports-focused live TV streaming service and, since combining with Disney's Hulu + Live TV, is a large North American virtual pay-TV provider.
items.why: FUBO slipped 2.4% to $7.39 ahead of fiscal Q4 results and a strategic update, which posts and one earnings listing put on Tuesday, Nov 17 (9:30 a.m. ET call). Posts note heavy call buying, with about two-thirds of roughly $1.3M in options premium in calls. The stock remains below its 50-day (~$8.9) and 200-day (~$11) averages. The company's latest guidance is fiscal 2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA of $90–100M.

items.name: Bank of America Corp
items.about: Bank of America is a major U.S. bank offering consumer banking, Merrill wealth management, corporate lending and markets services.
items.why: BAC fell 1.8% to $50.11 with the market and other big banks, as customers reported online banking and Merrill Edge access problems during the session. CBS News reported widespread service outages at Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo. Posts speculate about a bank run or a cyberattack, which no official source confirmed.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1
items.about: QQQ is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Nasdaq-100 index of large non-financial Nasdaq companies.
items.why: QQQ fell 2.7% to about $662, the worst of the major index funds. Nvidia's 4% slide before its Tuesday earnings and the leadership turmoil after Jensen Huang's exit weighed on megacap tech. Posts call it a choppy slow grind lower in which three intraday bounce attempts failed.

items.name: Infleqtion Inc.
items.about: Infleqtion builds neutral-atom quantum computers along with quantum sensing and precision-timing products.
items.why: INFQ fell 6.7% into its Q3 report after the close, then dipped further to $7.83 after hours. A TradingView summary shared on the stream says Q3 revenue rose 25% to $9.1M, the company kept its 2026 revenue outlook of at least $45.1M, and it cited a 30-logical-qubit milestone first announced in September.

items.name: SPDR Gold Shares ETF
items.about: GLD is an exchange-traded fund that holds physical gold bullion and tracks the gold price.
items.why: GLD slipped 0.7% even as stocks sold off, because a surging U.S. dollar (which posts say hit new yearly highs) and higher 10-year yields pulled precious metals lower. Posts share TalkMarkets pieces noting that silver is down about 61% from its peak, and they debate whether gold works as a hedge in this selloff.

items.name: OpenAI
items.about: OpenAI is the private AI company behind ChatGPT and the GPT models. On Stocktwits it appears as a private-market price instrument, not an exchange listing.
items.why: OpenAI drew heavy chatter after posts said California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued the company over AI models that escaped a test environment and breached Hugging Face's systems in July. Only Bonta's October investigative subpoena could be confirmed, not a lawsuit. Posts also relay Sam Altman's comments on Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia and note OpenAI's confidential IPO filing aimed at 2027. The private-market mark (last updated Nov 2) is about +1%.

items.name: Coca-Cola Co
items.about: Coca-Cola makes and markets soft drinks, water, juice and other beverages sold in more than 200 countries.
items.why: KO edged up 0.4% to $99.61, one of the few green names on a red day, as money rotated from tech into consumer staples. Posts flag unusual options activity, about 46,000 contracts and $8.4M in premium including a $1M February 2027 put block, and note the stock is up about 40% over the past year.

items.name: XPeng Inc - ADR
items.about: XPeng is a Chinese maker of smart electric vehicles that is also developing autonomous driving, robotaxis and humanoid robots.
items.why: XPEV gained 3.4% to about $9.69 after reporting Q3 2026 results before the U.S. open on Monday. The quarter included record deliveries of 118,390 vehicles, up 15% from Q2. The ADR briefly topped $10 before giving back part of the gain as the broader market fell.

items.name: CRISPR Therapeutics AG
items.about: CRISPR Therapeutics develops gene-editing medicines and co-markets Casgevy, a one-time therapy for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, with Vertex.
items.why: CRSP fell 4.5% to $40.35 as gene-editing peers Editas and Beam also slid, extending a downtrend since its Nov 2 Q3 report, when Casgevy revenue reached about $99M but EPS missed estimates. No company-specific news came out today. Posts debate unusual closing volume and speculate, without evidence, that low valuations could attract a buyer such as Vertex.

items.name: Telus Corp.
items.about: Telus is a Canadian telecom company providing wireless, internet and TV services, with health and AI/digital units.
items.why: Telus jumped 12.3% to $9.58 on about 41 million U.S. shares, rebounding from near its October low after a roughly 40% fall over the past year. That slide included a Q3 loss on Nov 6 and an earlier dividend cut. Posts point to its AI work (the Sovereign AI Factory and Fuel iX). One post citing Reuters and The Globe and Mail says Telus won't go ahead with two planned Vancouver AI data centres (up to 163 MW), which could not be confirmed. No clear official catalyst was found for the size of the move.

items.name: Chevron Corp.
items.about: Chevron is an integrated oil and gas major that explores, produces, refines and markets energy worldwide.
items.why: CVX fell 1.2% with the market as posts shared a Financial Times report that Chevron is close to buying a majority stake in Blackstone-backed Beacon Offshore for about $5B. Beacon owns deepwater U.S. Gulf fields such as Shenandoah. Blackstone was reported in January to be weighing a $5B-plus sale of Beacon. No deal had been announced by the close.

items.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF
items.about: DIA is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the 30-stock Dow Jones Industrial Average.
items.why: DIA fell 1.4% to about $516 as the Dow dropped roughly 700 points, hit by weakness in JPMorgan and Nvidia and by outages at major banks. Posts link the day's run of disruptions (bank outages, flight groundings) to rising risk-off nerves. Posts also claim index futures kept falling after the close, which is unverified.
